thread:
talia: quick flag 1 - brought up aurora-int8-v1 in streaming for toolcall smoke. seeing ~0.6% parse_fail on last 3k calls. pattern looks like stray control/escape sequences and occasional null-byte (\u0000) near chunk boundaries.

brad: example paste? streaming-only?

talia: streaming. snippet from raw chunks:

```
...
{"action":"notify","params":{"msg":"disk issue\\u0000retry?","tags":["infra","urgent"]}}
```
last chunk sometimes carries the literal null escape or a truncated escape like `\\u000`.

inna: if stream cuts in the middle of a unicode escape it will break our JSON parser. we should see if this is generation-level (model emits incomplete escapes) or framing-level (chunk cut mid-escape).

samir: good catch. fp16 baseline streaming for same prompts is ~0.02%. int8 batch ~0.05%. streaming+int8 shows the bump. propose: 1) capture raw byte-aligned chunks (not utf-8 decoded) so we can detect cut inside escape sequences; 2) add a stitcher stage that buffers when final bytes end with a partial escape sequence or backslash; 3) disable retry-on-parse-fail for canary to avoid duplicate tool calls.

talia: I'll enqueue a canary run with raw chunk capture (5k) and fixed seed. will log last-8 bytes of each chunk to help classify.

stitcher-bot: scheduled canary run: /ci/canary/6311112222/aurora-int8-v1 (5k). will post report to /ci/reports/6311112222.json.

brad: stitcher heuristic idea: if chunk ends with `\\` or `\\u` or `\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{0,3}` then hold for TTL=120ms and wait for next chunk; if next chunk completes escape, emit; else if TTL expires, try best-effort repair: complete truncated `\\u` with safe replacement char and tag as "stitcher_fixed_escape". we must log every repair.

inna: add metric 'escape_stitch_rate' and 'escape_auto_fix_rate' and tag repaired cases so they don't count as parse_fail-induced retries. also gate repairs: only auto-fix if truncated escape occurs in final 6 chars and overall structure otherwise valid.

samir: parallel experiment: run a transport check to ensure chunk framing doesn't drop bytes. compare raw chunk bytes between fp16 and int8 streams for same seed to see if frames differ before decoding. checksum-diff between raw chunks will tell us if model output differs vs transport artifacts.

talia: I've paused streaming rollout and switched aurora-int8-v1 to buffered fallback on canary. started the raw-capture run.

stitcher-bot: report posted: /ci/reports/6311112222.json (streaming_parse_fail:0.58%, buffered:0.07%, escape_stitch_rate:0.22%, escape_auto_fix_rate:0.15%, duplicate_invokes:+0.4pp). raw-chunk checksum diff shows most diffs start at token ~30 in failing cases.

brad: token ~30 divergence hints generation-level distortion. still the escape pattern suggests model might emit escapes differently under quantization. next: try quant variant with mixed-precision for first 6 layers vs last6 to see where escape tokenization shifts.

inna: also run small synthetic test where model is prompted to emit long unicode escapes and varied nested arrays to maximize chance of cutting escape sequences. compare per-byte outputs.

samir: I'll spin up an ablation grid: variants = [per-channel-scale, mixed-precision-last6, clamp-tweak] running 1k samples each and report parse_fail + escape_stitch_rate + p95 latency.

talia: filed INF-4120 and assigned to @samir and @brad. will update with results. thanks all. :sparkles:
